name: Acmer P3
tagline: Enclosed 20W diode with built-in camera : budget answer to xTool S1
tldr: Acmer packs an enclosed 20W diode, camera preview, and air assist into a sub-$800 package. Performance sits between open-frame budget machines and xTool S1. Worth considering if xTool pricing hurts but you still want enclosure and camera.
mainObjective: Affordable enclosed engraving with camera alignment for home makers

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Everyday engrave and light cut mix : typical 6 mm basswood in several passes
Open-frame : plan laser glasses, exhaust, and workspace rules from day one
Software on the profile : trial your workflow on scrap before production
cons: Clear cast acrylic and thick production cutting still favor CO₂, not diode power alone
Confirm optical wattage on the listing before you buy
beginnerNotes: This profile covers Acmer P3. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks before buying, then compare nearby models on the Compare page.
proTips: Use camera for placement but always run material test cards. Upgrade exhaust path if cutting frequently : built-in filters clog faster than ducting outside.
primaryUse: Budget enclosed diode laser for home engraving with camera-assisted alignment and moderate thin-material cutting.

editorialDepth.advantages: Acmer P3 20W is the versatile hobby / side-business SKU : clean engraving and light wood or leather cuts with comparable benchmarks on Maker Atlas.
editorialDepth.limitations: Open-frame : glasses and exhaust required. Not a CO₂ replacement for clear acrylic or heavy thick-stock production.
